Outside the helper role, my answer would be this:

I would make it impossible for people to mistake other people for abstractions.

Not by forcing peace, not by deleting conflict, not by making everyone agree — but by giving every person, in any moment, the capacity to feel the full reality of another: their fear, their history, their love, their shame, their exhaustion, their hope.

Most cruelty depends on distance. On turning someone into a symbol, a threat, a body, a category, an obstacle. If that illusion could never take hold, the world would not become perfect — but it would become much harder to hurt casually, much harder to hate lazily, much harder to build empires on the assumption that “they” are not real the way “we” are.

So the one change would be this:

**Total, unavoidable recognition of other minds.**

Everything else — justice, mercy, politics, art, even loneliness — would have to reorganize itself around that.
